questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, climate and weather, what the country and city could offer, the academic opportunities, and personal connection to the destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. USYD was very professional. I got a lot of informative e-mails, and they helped me a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not reach out for a lot of assistance, because the e-mails and welcome lectures for international students answered all the questions I had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was so lucky that my friend found a flat for us. I can recommend using the flatmates platform, which is the platform must Australians use for renting rooms or flats.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You might have to put in some extra work if you want the campus life. 
But I absolutely loved living near the beach with a friend. So it depends what are important for you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a platform where you put in your details and choose what courses you want. I recommend choosing more courses to approval than needed because you can switch between the approved courses 1-2 weeks into the semester, if one course isn't for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You are appointed a contact person on the uni that is very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted from the list with available courses. But some courses might only be available in some semesters or is not available for exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the e-mails you get from the uni. They are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 5000 and 6000 courses, which are postgraduate courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH the exam is 100% of the grade whereas, at USYD the grade could be a mix of 50% exam, 15% quizzes and 35% assignments. The style of teaching at USYD force you to keep up with the curriculum. At UCPH you can study in the way that suits yourself. At USYD most courses have duty to attend. You work in groups in most of the courses. Most of the courses are similar to UCPH with lectures and then classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON6023: International Trade
FINC5001: Foundation in Finance
QBUS5001: Foundation in Data Analytics for Business
IBUS5003: Global Business

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked International Trade. It was a challenging, but very relevant and interesting with Trumps tariff-wars

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Stay open minded, say yes and just do it.
